slices.focus: Podcast on legal language restarts reading habit
slices.summary: A friend (Yesenia) sends Lucia a podcast episode about legal language and wrongful convictions, which reignites her dormant reading habit. She shifts to one-book-at-a-time (narrative nonfiction about law, language, and system failures), reading in short 20-minute bursts rather than waiting for perfect conditions. The conversation covers her shift from a guilty half-read stack to a manageable singular book, keeping a finished-title list on an index card, and accepting that her reading taste naturally circles justice and institutional blind spots. The quieter stretch allows her to distinguish between wanting to read and wanting to collapse.
